newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-ELS EYES A LONG-RUNNING RIVALRY WITH WOODS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ELS EYES A LONG-RUNNING RIVALRY WITH WOODS.

text.p: Ernie Els is eager to get on with what he reckons will be a long-running rivalry with young Tiger Woods when the PGA Championship starts up on Thursday.

A tantalizing threesome of Masters champion Woods, U.S. Open champion Els and British Open winner Justin Leonard has been arranged for the first two rounds of the PGA, bringing together a leading trio of golf's "now" generation.

"If you look into the future, Tiger's going to be around for a very long time and hopefully myself. And hopefully we'll be playing together a lot in the future," Els, 27, said on the eve of the opening round.
Woods, 21, said Tuesday he was also looking forward to the threesome.
"It's going to be neat to see because we're going to be playing against each other for about 20 years and that's going to be really neat," Woods said.
The 25-year-old Leonard admitted there would be "a little bit more tension on our group than I have been used to in the past. You know there's going to be a lot of people out there."
Still, the steely Texan said he expected a good time.
"They're two good guys. They've got two great caddies. And the six of us should have a lot of fun."
Els, who considers himself the elder of the emerging group of stars that also includes Phil Mickelson, 27, took pains to point out that a 'rivalry' does not get personal in golf.

"I personally want to go out there and play as best as I can and if on that day I beat Tiger or Justin, whoever it might be, so be it," he said. "This is not like tennis where you play directly against the guy on the other side of the net.

"We've got 156 players (actually 150) here this week and you have to beat those players and you have to beat the golf course. And the golf course comes first, in my mind. If I feel I played a good round on the golf course, I will feel really happy about it. And if somebody does better than me, what can you do?
"I'm just going to try and play as good as I can and the same probably goes for Tiger and Justin and Phil Mickelson and the rest of the gang."
Els expects a gruelling test at Winged Foot, a course he says is tougher than both Oakmont and Congressional, the scenes of his U.S. Open triumphs.

Softened conditions from occasional showers on Wednesday may provide the players with a chance to go well under par in the first round, but par should be considered a very good score otherwise, agreed Els, Woods and Leonard.
Els differs with Woods on one subject, however. The runaway Masters winner said the old guard of golf stars was on the way out, falling victim to Father Time. Els thinks not.

"How do you define 'older players'? Do you define Greg Norman as an older player?" Els said for starters, using as an example the 42-year-old Australian, a two-time British Open champion ranked third in the world behind Els and No. 1 Woods.
"I don't believe that. I think Greg's got a lot of years ahead of him. If you look at the guys that just turned 40 now, if you call them older players, I don't want to insult them.
"I played a practice round this morning with Nick Price (40) and he's hitting the ball as good as ever."

Els said the success of the younger players may be motivating the established stars. "I don't think the older guys are through. They're working out in gyms and they're working on their bodies and on their physiques and everything, so they've got a couple of years ahead of them."
The South African took his thesis one step further.
"These guys have got experience. And I believe a great experienced player will win this week."
